title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 1st Truth Applying The Principle To The Cosmos

questions.question: What basic rule is explained by the examples of a book and a house?
questions.answer: A work points to an action, and that action points to a maker behind it.

questions.question: In this passage, what does a beautifully written book show beyond itself?
questions.answer: It shows that there was writing, a writer, and the skill needed for writing.

questions.question: What does a well-made house help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It shows that there was building, a builder, and the ability to build.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are names like writer and builder connected to qualities?
questions.answer: Such names require real abilities and traits that fit those names.

questions.question: Why does the passage say an attribute cannot exist by itself?
questions.answer: Because a quality must belong to someone who truly has it.

questions.question: What is the connection between a craft and a craftsman in the passage?
questions.answer: A craft proves that there is someone practicing that craft.

questions.question: How is the universe described after this principle is given?
questions.answer: It is described like many meaningful writings and many constructed buildings.

questions.question: What do all beings, separately and together, do according to the passage?
questions.answer: They give witness in many ways to the One behind them.

questions.question: Why are both single beings and all beings together mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that the evidence appears in each part and becomes even stronger in the whole.

questions.question: What two everyday examples are used to teach the main idea in this passage?
questions.answer: A meaningful book and a strongly made house.

questions.question: What act is connected to the existence of a book?
questions.answer: The act of writing.

questions.question: What act is connected to the existence of a house?
questions.answer: The act of building.

questions.question: After acts like writing and building, what comes next in the chain of reasoning?
questions.answer: The names or titles of the one who does those acts.

questions.question: After the names of writer and builder, what does the passage say must also exist?
questions.answer: The skills and qualities related to those jobs.

questions.question: After skills and qualities, what final conclusion does the passage reach?
questions.answer: There must be a real person who possesses them.

questions.question: Which impossible things are rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: A deed without a doer, a name without someone it belongs to, an attribute without a possessor, and a craft without a craftsman.

questions.question: How does this reasoning prepare the reader to think about the universe?
questions.answer: It teaches that the world also points beyond itself to its Maker.

questions.question: What does it mean that the universe is like many books and letters?
questions.answer: Its creatures carry signs, meaning, and messages that can be read.

questions.question: What does it mean that the universe is like many buildings and palaces?
questions.answer: Its parts are arranged with strength, design, and purpose.

questions.question: How does a beautiful piece of writing lead the mind step by step to a real writer?
questions.answer: It points to writing, then to the title of writer, then to writing ability, and finally to the one who has that ability.

questions.question: How does the house example support the same lesson as the book example?
questions.answer: Both show that a finished work proves purposeful action and a maker behind it.

questions.question: What role do names such as writer and builder play in the argument?
questions.answer: They link the visible work to the person known for doing that kind of work.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the difference between an act and an attribute?
questions.answer: An act is something done, while an attribute is a quality or ability in the one doing it.

questions.question: Why is it important that the passage mentions both attributes and crafts?
questions.answer: It strengthens the point that both qualities and skilled work require a real possessor.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the universe and written things?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to many meaningful texts.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the universe and constructed things?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to many carefully made structures.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase that beings testify alone and together?
questions.answer: Every creature is a sign by itself, and all creation together gives even greater proof.

questions.question: What is the first link in the reasoning chain presented in this passage?
questions.answer: A visible work, like a book or a house.

questions.question: What is the second link after the visible work?
questions.answer: The action that produced it, such as writing or building.

questions.question: What is the third link after the action?
questions.answer: The title or name of the one who does that action.

questions.question: What is the fourth link after the title?
questions.answer: The skill or quality needed for that work.

questions.question: What is the fifth and final link in the chain?
questions.answer: The actual being who possesses those skills and qualities.

questions.question: How is the universe pictured in relation to Divine Determining?
questions.answer: It is pictured like writings measured and set down with precision.

questions.question: How is the universe pictured in relation to Divine Power?
questions.answer: It is pictured like structures brought into existence with strength and ability.

questions.question: What does the word testimony mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means evidence or witness that points to a truth.

questions.question: What truth are the beings in the universe testifying to?
questions.answer: They are pointing to their Creator and Maker.

questions.question: What lesson is taught through the example of a deep and beautiful book?
questions.answer: Such a book could not exist without intentional writing and a writer.

questions.question: What lesson is taught through the example of a strongly built house?
questions.answer: Such a house could not exist without building and a builder.

questions.question: Why are writer and builder called names or titles in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they describe the one known by those actions.

questions.question: What must exist before someone can truly be called a writer or builder?
questions.answer: The needed abilities and qualities for that work must exist.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from qualities to a real person?
questions.answer: Because qualities cannot float by themselves; they need someone who has them.

questions.question: How does the passage use logic to support belief?
questions.answer: It shows that reason itself leads from created things to their maker.

questions.question: What two large pictures of the universe are given in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: A set of meaningful writings and a set of grand structures.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the number of signs in creation?
questions.answer: They are extremely many, both in each thing and in everything together.

questions.question: What brief statement best sums up the passage?
questions.answer: Creation is full of signs that point clearly to its Creator.

questions.question: In this passage, why can’t a deed exist without a doer?
questions.answer: Because every action must come from someone who performs it.

questions.question: Why can’t a name exist without one who is called by it?
questions.answer: Because a title must belong to a real possessor.

questions.question: Why can’t an attribute exist without one qualified by it?
questions.answer: Because a quality needs a real being in whom it exists.

questions.question: Why can’t a craft exist without a craftsman?
questions.answer: Because skillful work requires someone who practices that skill.

questions.question: How do these four impossible cases strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: They show from several angles that effects always point to a source.

questions.question: After giving this rule, how does the passage apply it to the universe?
questions.answer: It says the whole universe is like meaningful writing and careful construction.

questions.question: What does the phrase about Divine Determining suggest about creation?
questions.answer: It suggests measured planning and exact arrangement.

questions.question: What does the phrase about Divine Power suggest about creation?
questions.answer: It suggests the strength and ability by which things are brought into being.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about each created thing by itself?
questions.answer: Each one is a sign that gives evidence.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about all created things taken together?
questions.answer: Together they form a far greater and countless witness.
